title: Relative homotopy lifting for a simplicial left fibration
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices and degreewise products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], in fixed universes. Let $p:E\to B$ be any small left fibration, let $A\subseteq K$ be any degreewise injective inclusion of small simplicial sets, and put $V=(K\times\{0\})\cup_{A\times\{0\}}(A\times\Delta^1)\subseteq K\times\Delta^1$. Given simplicial maps $u:V\to E$ and $h:K\times\Delta^1\to B$ satisfying $pu=h|_V$, there exists a simplicial map $\widetilde h:K\times\Delta^1\to E$ with $\widetilde h|_V=u$ and $p\widetilde h=h$. No Kan or quasicategory hypothesis on $B,K,A,E$, no nonemptiness hypothesis, and no uniqueness of the lift is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.2.7, applied to the left horn {0} = Lambda_0^1 in Delta^1 and A in K; equivalently Corollary 2.1.2.10, the homotopy extension lifting property, printed pp.64-65. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text:
Let $e:\{0\}=\Lambda_0^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and let $j:V\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^1$ be the displayed inclusion. Use the opposite operation in clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]: $X^{\mathrm{op}}_n=X_n$, with an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ acting as $\alpha^r(t)=n-\alpha(m-t)$. Since $(\alpha^r)^r=\alpha$ and reversal respects composition, this is an involutive functor. Its degreewise sets are unchanged; hence it preserves degreewise products and pushout equivalence relations, and preserves degreewise injectivity. The standard-simplex isomorphism $r_n:(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^n$ sends a degree-$m$ simplex $\beta$ to $\beta^r(t)=n-\beta(m-t)$. It carries $(\Lambda_i^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ onto $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, since omitted vertices are reversed. In particular it carries $\{0\}^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1$. After $r_1$ and interchanging the two product factors, $j^{\mathrm{op}}$ becomes exactly
$$(\{1\}\times K^{\mathrm{op}})\amalg_{\{1\}\times A^{\mathrm{op}}}(\Delta^1\times A^{\mathrm{op}})\longrightarrow\Delta^1\times K^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
The first factor inclusion is a generating right horn and the other is a monomorphism. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] makes this map right anodyne. Its class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition (a finite transfinite composite), so the isomorphic arrow $j^{\mathrm{op}}$ is right anodyne as well.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.2.7 and the left/right horn duality; the pushout-product identification is written degreewise from the cylinder inclusion.

proof.text:
For $n\geq1$ and $0<k\leq n$, reversing a lifting square for $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ against $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ gives a square for $p$ against $\Lambda_{n-k}^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. Here $0\leq n-k<n$, so [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and the hypothesis that $p$ is a left fibration give a filler. Reverse this filler back. Hence $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a right fibration on arbitrary simplicial sets. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $p^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $j^{\mathrm{op}}$. It makes
$$\rho:\operatorname{Fun}((K\times\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}},E^{\mathrm{op}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}((K\times\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}},B^{\mathrm{op}})\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(V^{\mathrm{op}},B^{\mathrm{op}})}\operatorname{Fun}(V^{\mathrm{op}},E^{\mathrm{op}})$$
a trivial Kan fibration. The equality $pu=h|_V$ says exactly that $(h^{\mathrm{op}},u^{\mathrm{op}})$ is a vertex of its target. Vertex surjectivity in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] gives a vertex $H:(K\times\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}\to E^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $p^{\mathrm{op}}H=h^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $Hj^{\mathrm{op}}=u^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.2.7, applied to the left horn {0}=Lambda_0^1; equivalently Corollary 2.1.2.10, homotopy extension lifting property.

proof.text: Take $\widetilde h=H^{\mathrm{op}}$ using the strict double-opposite identification of step 1. Reversing the two equalities of step 2 gives $p\widetilde h=h$ and $\widetilde h j=u$ exactly. The domain of $j$ is the stated union $V$: in degree $m$ the two subsets $K_m\times\{0\}$ and $A_m\times(\Delta^1)_m$ intersect in $A_m\times\{0\}$, so their pushout is their union; these identifications commute with every simplicial operator. Thus the extension fixes all prescribed data. If $K=\varnothing$ the lift is the unique empty map; if $A=K$, $j$ is the identity and the lift is $u$. If $A=\varnothing$, step 1 still applies to the monomorphism $\varnothing\to K$. Empty $E$ causes no problem: whenever compatible data $(u,h)$ exist they give the target vertex used in step 2. No Kan or quasicategory hypothesis or uniqueness assertion enters.

source.place: Corollary 2.1.2.10, explicit relative boundary identification and edge cases.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 2.1.2.7 and Corollary 2.1.2.10, expanded by opposite duality and the existing right-anodyne pushout-product/exponential lifting nodes; online source not archived.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q65-b85111ccb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The delivery is one commit with the item and its report, and no new nodes. Statement: this is the HTT 2.1.2.7/2.1.2.10 lifting property: the pushout product of {0}->Delta^1 with a monomorphism A ⊆ K lifts against any left fibration of arbitrary simplicial sets. I tested it on K empty, A=K, A empty with K a point (which is exactly the Lambda^1_0 lifting in the definition), and E empty. I also checked that the endpoint orientation matters: with the final endpoint the statement fails for the left fibration {1}->Delta^1. The citer, straightening step 5 (K=E arbitrary, A=X_c), uses it within its hypotheses. Step 1: the opposite operation from relative-cone-equivalence clause (4) uses the same reversal formula and is an automorphism of sSet; r_n is simplicial and sends the opposite of Lambda^n_i to Lambda^n_{n-i}, so {0}^op goes to {1}=Lambda^1_1, a right horn. j^op is literally the pushout product in right-anodyne-product with i=Lambda^1_1 and k=A^op->K^op. Closure under isomorphisms and composition covers the isomorphic arrow. Step 2: the horn index ranges reverse correctly, so p^op is a right fibration. The exponentiation node allows arbitrary small simplicial sets. (h^op,u^op) is a target vertex, and vertex surjectivity (Stacks 08NL, simplicial.tex lines 5533-5545) gives an exact lift. Step 3 is genuinely elementary: the pushout equals the union degree by degree, and taking opposites twice returns the original maps. I found no cycle in the transitive closure, and all cited statements are in the same unit, so no tool_uses are needed. I searched the DAG for left-anodyne, cylinder, pushout-product and fibration-exponentiation nodes and found no duplicate. No SGA is used. HTT and Kerodon are online only, so I could not check them from literature/; they are recorded as WANTED, with proof_origin set to agent. No changes made.
